key_insight: PEA organic spacers improve morphology and suppress lattice defects in 2D lead iodide perovskites, slowing degradation under ambient light and thermal stress compared with BA spacers.
engineering_relevance: Spacer selection can improve perovskite durability, but long-term device stability also requires structural and chemical engineering, surface passivation, and encapsulation.
method: Compared BA2PbI4 and PEA2PbI4 perovskite nanoflakes.
Assessed ambient light and thermal degradation.
Used confocal micro-Raman and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy.
evidence_signal: Freshly exfoliated samples showed comparable room-temperature luminescence; both lost organic components and decomposed into PbI2 and metallic Pb, but PEA samples degraded more slowly.
watch_item: The abstract reports material-level stability rather than solar-cell efficiency or device lifetime, so performance–stability trade-offs remain unresolved.
paper_title: Impact of organic spacer cations on the light and thermal stability of two-dimensional lead halide perovskites
